text.title: Rails 7+ Backend Examples
text.summary: Worked example: bringing an Orders module back onto Rails conventions — resourceful routes, Strong Parameters, side effects out of callbacks and secrets into encrypted credentials — plus the routes and controller shapes it produces.

example.context: Rails 7 app. `OrdersController` is reached through eight ad-hoc routes; `Order` carries `after_create :send_confirmation_email`; the Stripe key is read from ENV; `create` mass-assigns `params[:order]`.
example.walk: Step 1: audit the module — 8 ad-hoc routes, 1 side-effect callback, 1 ENV secret, 1 unpermitted mass assignment. Step 2: `config/routes.rb` collapses to `resources :orders` with `member { patch :cancel; post :refund }` and a `collection { get :recent }`, so `cancel_order_path` exists again. Step 3: the controller grows a private `order_params` returning `params.require(:order).permit(:note, items_attributes: %i[sku qty])`, and every action uses it. Step 4: the mailer call moves from the `Order` callback into `OrderService#confirm`, which the controller invokes explicitly; the callback is deleted. Step 5: `rails credentials:edit` takes `stripe.secret`, the call site becomes `Rails.application.credentials.stripe[:secret]`, and the ENV var leaves the deploy script.
example.output: Eight routes become one `resources` block plus two member routes; a console `touch` no longer mails a customer; the secret no longer appears in an exception dump; unpermitted attributes never reach the model.

example.code:
Rails.application.routes.draw do namespace :api do namespace :v1 do resources :orders, only: %i[index show create update destroy] do member do patch :cancel post :refund end
collection { get :recent }
resources :items, only: %i[index show create destroy], shallow: true end
resource :session, only: %i[create destroy] resources :users, only: %i[show update] end end
get "/health", to: "health#show" root "home#index" end
example.note: Non-CRUD verbs live inside the resource as `member` / `collection`, so they keep named helpers — `restful-resources`.

example.code:
class Api::V1::OrdersController < Api::V1::BaseController before_action :set_order, only: %i[show update destroy cancel refund]
def index @orders = policy_scope(Order).includes(:items).recent render json: OrderResource.from_collection(@orders) end
def create result = Orders::CreateService.new(params: order_params, current_user: current_user).call return render json: { errors: result.errors }, status: :unprocessable_entity if result.failure?
render json: OrderResource.from(result.value), status: :created end
private
def set_order @order = Order.find(params[:id]) end
def order_params params.require(:order).permit(:note, items_attributes: %i[sku qty]) end end
example.note: Strong Parameters at the boundary, the service returning the shared `ServiceResult`, eager-loading at the controller — the architecture rules and the convention rules meeting in one class.
